newsitem.title: USA: Texaco buys large portion of Canada oil.
newsitem.headline: Texaco buys large portion of Canada oil.

text.p: Texaco Inc bought nearly 70 percent of crude oil offered in an unusually large Canadian spot sale late Thursday, an industry source said.
About 500,000 barrels of "distressed" Koch Alberta crude, a light sour grade, was sold to Texaco's refinery in Anacortes, Washington.
"It's quite a bit cheaper (compared with sales in the last six months)," the source said, declining to give the price.
Canadian crude producers have been stuck with excess light sours as a result of heavy maintenance work on Canada's large Interprovincial Pipe Line Inc system this autumn.

Around 120,000 barrels will be delivered to the refinery in mid September via the Trans Mountain Pipe Line Co Ltd based in Vancouver, Canada. Another 380,000 barrels will be sent over the line in mid-October.
Texaco bought the grade at a slight premium to Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude, a staple of the West Coast market.
The Anacortes refinery, which can process 143,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude, gets more for their money by taking the Canadian grade, the source claimed.
"It's a little lighter and the refinery sees a little more value in it," the source said.
Around 250,000 barrels of the Canadian crude remains available for sale, but marketers apparently want to sell it outside the West Coast, where low prices for ANS have undercut prices for imports.
"They want to move it out of the PADD (West Coast region) and go foreign with it," the source said.
